environment.description: Same binary deployed in a hardened container orchestrated via Kubernetes. The pod spec includes a custom seccomp profile (runtime/default augmented with a deny-list) that restricts the brk/mmap/mremap family to only allow allocations below 128MB total RSS via a cgroup memory.max of 134217728 bytes AND the container uses a custom LD_PRELOAD allocator (scudo from LLVM compiler-rt) compiled with quarantine_size_kb=4096 and dealloc_type_mismatch=true. The pgBouncer instance (v1.21) sits between the app and PostgreSQL with server_lifetime=300, max_client_conn=4, and prepared statement mode (pool_mode=statement with disable_pqexec=1), meaning parameterized queries are parsed and re-prepared per transaction, limiting the window for heap corruption to propagate into connection state. The combination of scudo's quarantine (which delays reuse of freed pages for 4MB worth of allocations), the strict RSS limit (which causes OOM-kill before heap spray can fill the quarantine), and the connection pooler's statement-mode isolation (which tears down server-side state between queries, preventing corrupted buffers from persisting across query boundaries) collectively neutralize the double-free exploitation path.

config.allocator: scudo (LLVM compiler-rt) via LD_PRELOAD, quarantine_size_kb=4096, dealloc_type_mismatch=true
